chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Murazim, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Musadif, his slave: 'Acquire a piece of land or a property, for when a calamity or misfortune befalls a man, and he remembers that behind his back there is something to support his family, he becomes more generous with himself.'

key_terms.عُقْدَة: A piece of land or property

ai.seo_question: Why should a Muslim invest in real estate according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises his slave Musadif to acquire real estate or property, emphasizing its role as a financial safety net. This investment serves to support his family during hardships, enabling him to be more generous and less stingy with himself. The hadith highlights the importance of securing one's family's future through tangible assets, which in turn fosters a spirit of generosity and reduces anxiety in times of need.

en.hubeali: Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al nahdy, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Murazim, from his father who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to Musadif, a slave of his<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Take real estate or a place (house etc.), for the man, when there descends unto him an affliction or the difficulty, so he remembers that behind his back is what his family can stand upon, he would be more generous with himself’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdiy from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Murazim from his father who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, once said to his Mawla’, Musadif, ‘Find some real property or goods; when man faces hardship or misfortune, and then finds out that behind him there is something for support of his family, he feels more generous to allow his soul to depart (his body).”’
